LESSON: FAMILY UNITY

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Creation
Topic 1.4: Family Unity

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Family Unity. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is family unity important?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe the importance of family unity
2. identify challenges faced by families today

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: FAMILY UNITY
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Family Unity helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: FAMILY UNITY
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Describe the importance of family unity

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the importance of family unity. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the importance of family unity.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Family Unity” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the importance of family unity. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Identify challenges faced by families today

What this means
In this part you learn to identify challenges faced by families today. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify challenges faced by families today.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to Family Unity.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify challenges faced by families today. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Family Unity is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “Family Unity” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: describe the importance of family unity)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to Family Unity. (skill: identify challenges faced by families today)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Family Unity to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe the importance of family unity.
3. Practise this skill: identify challenges faced by families today.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Family Unity from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Family Unity: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Family Unity?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is family unity important?
2. How can family unity be maintained?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Family Unity means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe the importance of family unity.
5. Be able to: identify challenges faced by families today.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
